description: Given a tab with a Chinese title and no Pillow installed, when its PDF is rendered, then it is refused unless lossy output is asked for, and written when it is.
Given the adopted repo, when its test script runs, then every bass-tab check passes.
Given the tracked files, when they are scanned for home-directory paths and personal email addresses, then none is found.

Given sources for a song, when the agent writes the song file, then each bar, chord and lyric comes only from a cited source, which a person reading the source report checks; the nightly run checks the report's format (BAS-8).
Given a song whose source shows only a title, when its chart is rendered, then the title prints, header fields with no value are left out, and a full song's fields print in template order.

Given a song with a source report, when its chart is rendered, then missing bars, estimates and the source per section print after the last stave line, a missing part reads "not shown", and a bad report key is refused.

Given a 5-string and a 4-string song, when each chart is rendered, then the first draws five stave lines labeled G D A E B and the second four labeled G D A E, and the text tab refuses the 5-string song.

Given a changed copy of the format template, when two songs are rendered through it, then the header order, missing text, repeat format, section size and line gap all follow it, and a bad template is refused by name.
Given the repo, when its workflows are listed, then no health.yml exists because health runs on the Mac.

Given a song with a missing bar, when its chart is rendered, then the bar is drawn as wide as the widest bar the song has and is marked "missing", and planning many missing bars stays linear in the song length.
Given a song with estimated bars, when its chart is rendered, then each estimated bar carries an estimate sign above it and no other bar does.
Given a song, when its chart is rendered, then every bar drawn prints its bar number.
Given a song with a tempo, when its chart is rendered, then each section label carries its start time, and a song with no tempo shows none.
Given a song with a section longer than one line, when its chart is rendered, then the next section starts on a new line and no line mixes a section tail with a new section.
Given a song with a repeated figure, when its chart is rendered, then the repeat count is centered above the closing repeat sign and clear of every chord name and every bar number.
Given a song that fits one page, when its chart is rendered, then its tab digits are larger than 10 pt, and a two-page song stays at 9 to 10 pt on two pages.
Given a song whose chorus repeats an earlier section, when its chart is rendered, then the repeat is one reference line by default and is drawn out with --expand-sections.
Given a song with no artist, key or report, when its chart is rendered, then those header fields and the all-not-shown report are left out, and a field with a value stays.

Given a song whose estimated bars equal a neighbour, when its chart is rendered, then every estimated bar is drawn with its own sign clear of the chord name, no repeat and no section reference swallows one, and a repeat before or after it still folds.

Given bars with identical notes under different chords, when the chart is rendered, then neither a repeat nor a section reference folds them and every chord name prints, while a chord named once for a repeated figure still folds.

Given reports that are absent, None, an empty map, empty lists or sources only, when the chart is rendered, then only an absent, None or empty-sections report is left out, an explicit empty list prints none, and a sources-only report stays visible.
Given a song whose first repeat sits beside a section label, when its chart is rendered, then no repeat count overlaps a section label or its start time.

Given a song with a long run of missing bars, a lone missing bar, missing bars that carry a chord or a lyric, and a run that reaches a section start, when its chart is rendered, then each run of two or more plain missing bars prints as one full-width line with its range, a lone or chord or lyric bar stays a bar, no run crosses a section, and a single missing bar renders as before.
Given a chart song with a Chinese lyric and no Pillow installed, when its PDF is rendered, then it is refused unless lossy output is asked for, and written when it is.
